subject: Re: Deployment mode for PHI workloads - HIPAA/BAA next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Gupta <samira.gupta@elarahealth.com>, Ian Thompson <ian.thompson@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Deployment options recap & next steps (HIPAA/BAA)

Hi Samira / Ian —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have alignment: 

Summary of needs you mentioned:
- Production will handle PHI (patient PII + claims) and requires a BAA.
- SOC 2 Type II evidence required for procurement review.
- Audit log access and data retention controls important for your security team.
- Preferred deployment: private/network-isolated option if we can meet timeline and audit requirements (you flagged Dedicated capacity + VPC or Private on-prem as possibilities).

Redwood deployment options we discussed:
1) Hosted API: fastest to get started; we can scope tokenization and pseudonymization but will not meet your default BAA requirements unless paired with contractual controls.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool + private VPC peering): gives isolation, customer-dedicated compute, and stronger network controls (recommended if you need predictable throughput and isolation).
3) Private (VPC or on-prem): full control over networking and key management (KMS/HSM) — best for strict regulatory or air-gapped needs but longer provisioning and procurement lead time.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Can you confirm whether PHI will ever be stored long-term vs just processed in-transit? (This impacts retention settings.)
- I'll attach our SOC 2 report and a draft BAA for your legal/security to review.
- If Dedicated/Private is required, please share any specific architecture constraints (e.g., must use your KMS, specific subnets, IP allowlist).

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2025.pdf (redacted), BAA_Draft_Elara_20260301.docx

Proposed timeline: if you confirm Dedicated/VPC by EOW, we can scope a deployment plan and preliminary pricing for reserved capacity in 3–4 business days; Private deployment would require 2–4 weeks for networking and legal setup depending on your IT team availability.

I'll coordinate with Dylan (solutions) and Rishi (security) to prepare detailed answers and a canary plan for the Dedicated path.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0184

From: Samira Gupta <samira.gupta@elarahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ian Thompson <ian.thompson@elarahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment options recap & next steps (HIPAA/BAA)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side: 
- We will be processing PHI (claims and notes). Data is not intended to be stored long-term in the model; mainly in-transit processing with logs retained for 90 days for audit.
- BAA is a hard requirement for procurement. We need an executed BAA in place before any production usage.
- SOC 2 Type II report is required for vendor approval; can you confirm the scope (are the infra + hosting controls included)?
- We prefer Dedicated capacity with VPC peering so we can control egress and maintain network isolation. Private on-prem is a blocker due to timeline — we don't have bandwidth for that right now.

Could you also confirm:
1) Whether Redwood supports bringing our KMS keys (we need CMEK for key separation).
2) What audit/logging access you provide (S3 exports, SIEM integration, retention controls).

If you can get a BAA and SOC2 scope + report to us early next week that would be ideal — our procurement has a 5-business-day turnaround once docs are received.

Appreciate it,
Samira
Senior Product Manager, Security & Compliance | Elara Health
samira.gupta@elarahealth.com

Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Elara - BAA & deployment asks (internal)

Dylan / Rishi — forwarding thread from Elara (Samira + Ian). Key asks: Dedicated capacity + VPC peering, BAA required, SOC2 Type II report scope confirmation, CMEK support, audit/log exports (90-day retention). Procurement timeline: 5 business days after docs come in.

Suggested plan:
- Rishi: can you confirm whether Redwood can support customer-managed KMS (CMEK) for Dedicated deployments? If not fully supported, can we provide a compensating control (dedicated keys + export restrictions)?
- Dylan: can you prepare a scoped Dedicated proposal (network diagram, proposed topology, pricing estimate for baseline reserved capacity) — aim for initial draft by EOD Thu 3/5. Include a canary fallback plan to Hosted API for non-PHI workloads during transition.
- I'll attach the redacted SOC2 report and BAA draft and open a Legal/Procurement thread. We should anticipate legal redlines on BAA.

Notes for responses: SOC2 report we attached covers our control environment for 2025 and includes hosting/infra controls (we'll confirm exact in-scope systems). Audit logs: we provide token-level logs and can export to S3 or stream to a customer SIEM for Dedicated. Retention configs are adjustable per-customer on Dedicated.

I'll loop Legal (cc'd when we have their inbox) if BAA redlines come back.

Thanks —
Marissa

Marissa / team —

Appreciate the fast follow. A few quick priorities from procurement/security so we can move forward: 
- Please send final SOC2 Type II report (full, not the redacted summary) and the BAA with track changes by next Wednesday (3/11).
- Confirm whether you support customer-managed keys (CMEK) for the Dedicated offering; if yes, we need a short runbook for key rotation and access controls.
- For audit/logging: we'd like S3 export + CloudWatch/Log streaming option and confirmation that logs include request IDs, timestamps, and token-level cost/latency metrics.
- Any reference customers in health care who have used Dedicated + VPC peering would be helpful for our risk review.

If you can provide the SOC2 and the BAA with a point-of-contact in Legal so we can circulate, procurement will start review immediately.

Thanks,
Ian Thompson
Director, Procurement | Elara Health
